$comment: Hand-curated column detail for the tables people actually query. Columns default to confidence 'community' (recalled/observed, not proven by a Stripe doc page); build_schema.py promotes any column that the doc extractor found in an official Stripe SQL example to 'documented'. Run tools/verify_against_sigma.py on a real account to promote the rest to 'verified'. Tables with columns_complete=false may have additional columns not listed here.

balance_transactions.description: Ledger-style record of every event that moves money into or out of your Stripe balance. The canonical starting point for accounting and reconciliation, because it covers charges, refunds, transfers, payouts, adjustments and fees in one immutable table.
balance_transactions.grain: One row per balance transaction. Rows are never mutated after creation.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed txn_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the transaction was created (UTC).

columns.name: available_on
columns.description: When the funds become available in your balance.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Gross amount in minor currency units. Negative for money leaving your balance.

columns.name: fee
columns.description: Total fee in minor units. Break it down via balance_transaction_fee_details.

columns.name: net
columns.description: amount minus fee, in minor units.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: source_id
columns.description: Polymorphic id of the object that caused this transaction. Resolve the target using the id prefix or the type column: ch_ -> charges, re_ -> refunds, po_/tr_ -> transfers.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Transaction type.

columns.name: reporting_category
columns.description: Coarser grouping of type, aligned with Stripe's financial reports. Prefer this over type for revenue reporting.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text description of the transaction.

columns.name: automatic_transfer_id
columns.description: The automatic payout this transaction was included in. Joins to transfers.id.

columns.name: exchange_rate
columns.description: Rate applied when the presentment currency differs from the settlement currency.

notes: Prefer this table over charges/refunds for anything accounting-related; it is the only table that nets out fees consistently.
source_id is polymorphic and has no single FK target. Join conditionally on type.
A charge and its refund are separate rows; refunding never mutates the original row.

balance_transaction_fee_details.description: Line-item breakdown of the fee column on balance_transactions.
balance_transaction_fee_details.grain: One row per fee component of a balance transaction. A balance transaction can have several.

columns.name: balance_transaction_id
columns.description: The balance transaction this fee component belongs to.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Fee component amount in minor currency units.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Kind of fee.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Human-readable description of the fee.

notes: Summing amount here reproduces balance_transactions.fee for the same balance transaction.

charges.description: One row per Charge object. Use for charge-level analysis such as card brand mix, decline reasons and fraud outcomes. For accounting totals use balance_transactions instead.
charges.grain: One row per charge, including failed charges.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed ch_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the charge was created (UTC).

columns.name: captured_at
columns.description: When the charge was captured. Null if never captured. Note the API exposes this as a boolean `captured`.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Charge amount in minor currency units.

columns.name: amount_refunded
columns.description: Amount refunded so far, in minor units.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Charge status.

columns.name: paid
columns.description: Whether the charge was successfully paid.

columns.name: refunded
columns.description: Whether the charge was fully refunded.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text description.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer the charge belongs to. Joins to customers.id.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Invoice that generated this charge, if any.

columns.name: payment_intent_id
columns.description: PaymentIntent that created this charge, if any.

columns.name: balance_transaction_id
columns.description: Balance transaction recording this charge's effect on your balance.

columns.name: dispute_id
columns.description: Dispute against this charge, if any.

columns.name: transfer_id
columns.description: Connect transfer generated by this charge (destination charges). Joins to transfers.id.

columns.name: destination_id
columns.description: Connected account funds were routed to. Joins to accounts.id / connected_accounts.id.

columns.name: transfer_group
columns.description: String grouping this charge with related transfers.

columns.name: application_fee_id
columns.description: Application fee collected by the platform, if any.

columns.name: failure_code
columns.description: Machine-readable decline code when status is failed, e.g. card_declined.

columns.name: failure_message
columns.description: Human-readable decline reason when status is failed.

columns.name: payment_method_id
columns.description: PaymentMethod used. Joins to payment_methods.id.

columns.name: payment_method_type
columns.description: Payment method family used, e.g. card, us_bank_account, sepa_debit.

columns.name: card_brand
columns.description: Card brand as displayed, e.g. Visa, MasterCard, American Express. Note the capitalization differs from the API's lowercase values.

columns.name: card_country
columns.description: Two-letter ISO country of the issuing bank. Compare against your own country to measure cross-border volume.

columns.name: card_funding
columns.description: Funding type.

columns.name: card_last4
columns.description: Last four digits of the card.

columns.name: card_cvc_check
columns.description: CVC verification result.

columns.name: card_address_zip_check
columns.description: Postal code verification result.

columns.name: outcome_type
columns.description: Radar's verdict.

columns.name: outcome_risk_score
columns.description: Radar risk score from 0 to 100. Higher is riskier.

columns.name: outcome_risk_level
columns.description: Bucketed risk level.

columns.name: outcome_rule_id
columns.description: Radar rule that produced the outcome. Joins to radar_rules.id.

columns.name: outcome_network_status
columns.description: How the card network responded, e.g. approved_by_network, declined_by_network.

columns.name: outcome_seller_message
columns.description: Plain-language explanation of the outcome.

columns.name: statement_descriptor
columns.description: Text shown on the cardholder's statement.

columns.name: receipt_email
columns.description: Email the receipt was sent to.

columns.name: livemode
columns.description: False for sandbox/test data.

notes: card_brand values are display-cased (Visa, MasterCard), not the API's lowercase (visa, mastercard). Filter accordingly.
Extra card detail beyond the flattened card_* columns lives in payment_method_details, joined on charge_id.
A partial capture produces both a charge for the full authorized amount and a refund with reason 'partial_capture'. Exclude those refunds when measuring true refund rates.

payment_method_details.description: Per-charge payment method detail that does not fit in the flattened card_* columns on charges, including 3D Secure results and wallet information.

columns.name: charge_id
columns.description: The charge these details describe.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Payment method family, e.g. card, us_bank_account.

columns.name: card_3ds_succeeded
columns.description: Whether 3D Secure authentication succeeded for this charge.

columns.name: card_3ds_authenticated
columns.description: Whether the cardholder completed 3DS authentication.

columns.name: card_wallet_type
columns.description: Wallet used, e.g. apple_pay, google_pay. Null when not a wallet payment.

columns.name: card_network
columns.description: Network that processed the payment.

notes: Left join from charges — not every charge has a row here.

refunds.description: One row per Refund object. Refunds are separate objects from charges; refunding a charge creates a row here and a matching balance transaction.
refunds.grain: One row per refund. A charge may have many partial refunds.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed re_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the refund was created (UTC).

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Refunded amount in minor currency units (positive here; the balance transaction is negative).

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: charge_id
columns.description: Charge being refunded.

columns.name: payment_intent_id
columns.description: PaymentIntent being refunded, if applicable.

columns.name: balance_transaction_id
columns.description: Balance transaction recording this refund.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: Why the refund was issued.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Refund status.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text description.

notes: reason = 'partial_capture' rows are an artifact of auth-and-capture, not customer refunds. Filter them out of refund-rate metrics.

disputes.description: One row per Dispute (chargeback), including any evidence you submitted.
disputes.grain: One row per dispute. A single charge can have more than one dispute, so count distinct dispute ids.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed dp_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the dispute was opened (UTC).

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Disputed amount in minor currency units.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: charge_id
columns.description: Charge being disputed.

columns.name: payment_intent_id
columns.description: PaymentIntent being disputed, if applicable.

columns.name: balance_transaction_id
columns.description: Balance transaction for the disputed funds and dispute fee.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: Reason given by the card network.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Dispute status. 'prevented' means Rapid Dispute Resolution stopped it before it became a chargeback.

columns.name: evidence_due_by
columns.description: Deadline for submitting evidence.

columns.name: is_charge_refundable
columns.description: Whether the underlying charge can still be refunded.

notes: Exclude status = 'prevented' when computing chargeback ratios the way card networks measure them.
Dispute data lags: recent months undercount because disputes arrive weeks after the charge.

early_fraud_warnings.description: Fraud reports issued by the card network before a formal dispute is filed. Leading indicator for card brand monitoring programs such as Visa VAMP.
early_fraud_warnings.grain: One row per early fraud warning.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed issfr_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the warning was received (UTC).

columns.name: charge_id
columns.description: Charge the warning is about.

columns.name: payment_intent_id
columns.description: PaymentIntent the warning is about, if applicable.

columns.name: fraud_type
columns.description: Type of fraud reported by the network.

columns.name: actionable
columns.description: Whether you can still act (for example refund) to avoid a chargeback.

customers.grain: One row per customer, including deleted ones.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed cus_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the customer was created (UTC).

columns.name: email
columns.description: Customer email address.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Customer full name.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text description.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Customer's default currency.

columns.name: delinquent
columns.description: Whether the latest invoice attempt failed.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Account credit balance in minor units. Negative means credit owed to the customer.

columns.name: default_source_id
columns.description: Default payment source.

columns.name: address_country
columns.description: Two-letter ISO country from the billing address.

columns.name: address_city
columns.description: City from the billing address.

columns.name: address_postal_code
columns.description: Postal code from the billing address.

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.description: Whether the customer has been deleted. Deleted customers remain in the table.

columns.name: livemode
columns.description: False for sandbox/test data.

notes: Deleted customers are retained here, so filter on is_deleted for active-customer counts.

payment_intents.description: One row per PaymentIntent. Represents the full lifecycle of collecting a payment, including attempts that never produced a charge.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed pi_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the intent was created (UTC).

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Intended amount in minor currency units.

columns.name: amount_received
columns.description: Amount actually collected, in minor units.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Intent status.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer the intent belongs to.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Invoice that created this intent, if any.

columns.name: payment_method_id
columns.description: PaymentMethod attached to the intent.

columns.name: capture_method
columns.description: When to capture funds.

columns.name: cancellation_reason
columns.description: Why the intent was canceled, if it was.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text description.

columns.name: livemode
columns.description: False for sandbox/test data.

notes: Use this table to measure checkout conversion and drop-off; charges only contains attempts that reached the network.

transfers.description: Payouts from your Stripe balance to your bank account, and — for Connect platforms — transfers of funds to connected accounts.
transfers.grain: One row per payout or transfer.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier. Payouts on/after 2017-04-06 use po_; earlier payouts and Connect transfers use tr_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the payout/transfer was created (UTC).

columns.name: date
columns.description: Scheduled arrival date of the payout in the destination account.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Amount in minor currency units.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, lowercase.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Payout status.

columns.name: destination_id
columns.description: Destination bank account, card, or connected account.

columns.name: transfer_group
columns.description: String grouping this transfer with the charges that funded it.

columns.name: automatic
columns.description: Whether this was an automatic payout. Only automatic payouts can be reconciled to specific balance transactions.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text description.

columns.name: failure_code
columns.description: Reason the payout failed, if it did.

notes: Reconcile a payout to its components with: balance_transactions.automatic_transfer_id = transfers.id.
Manual payouts cannot be reconciled to specific balance transactions — the amount is arbitrary.

accounts.description: Your own account and, for Connect platforms, your connected accounts.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed acct_.

columns.name: created
columns.description: When the account was created (UTC).

columns.name: country
columns.description: Two-letter ISO country of the account.

columns.name: default_currency
columns.description: Account's default currency. Commonly used as the reporting currency when converting multi-currency figures.

columns.name: email
columns.description: Account email address.

columns.name: business_name
columns.description: Business name on the account.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Connect account type.

columns.name: charges_enabled
columns.description: Whether the account can create charges.

columns.name: payouts_enabled
columns.description: Whether the account can receive payouts.

notes: Connect platforms also have a connected_accounts table with richer onboarding and requirements detail.

connected_accounts.description: Connect platform view of connected accounts, including legal entity, onboarding requirements and terms-of-service acceptance.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier, prefixed acct_.

columns.name: email
columns.description: Account email address.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Two-letter ISO country of the account.

columns.name: business_name
columns.description: Business name on the account.

columns.name: payouts_enabled
columns.description: Whether the account can receive payouts.

columns.name: legal_entity_type
columns.description: Legal entity type.

columns.name: legal_entity_first_name
columns.description: First name of the legal entity representative.

columns.name: legal_entity_last_name
columns.description: Last name of the legal entity representative.

columns.name: legal_entity_address_line1
columns.description: Street address of the legal entity.

columns.name: legal_entity_address_city
columns.description: City of the legal entity.

columns.name: legal_entity_address_state
columns.description: State/province of the legal entity.

columns.name: legal_entity_address_postal_code
columns.description: Postal code of the legal entity.

columns.name: legal_entity_dob_day
columns.description: Day of birth of the representative.

columns.name: legal_entity_dob_month
columns.description: Month of birth of the representative.

columns.name: legal_entity_dob_year
columns.description: Year of birth of the representative.

columns.name: legal_entity_ssn_last_4_provided
columns.description: Whether the last 4 SSN digits were provided.

columns.name: legal_entity_personal_id_number_provided
columns.description: Whether a personal ID number was provided.

columns.name: legal_entity_verification_document_id
columns.description: Identifier of the uploaded verification document.

columns.name: tos_acceptance_date
columns.description: When the account accepted the Stripe terms of service.

columns.name: tos_acceptance_ip
columns.description: IP address recorded at terms-of-service acceptance.

columns.name: requirements_currently_due
columns.description: Comma-separated requirements due now. Empty string when nothing is due — test with != '' rather than IS NOT NULL.

columns.name: requirements_past_due
columns.description: Comma-separated requirements already overdue.

columns.name: requirements_eventually_due
columns.description: Comma-separated requirements that will eventually be due.

columns.name: requirements_pending_verification
columns.description: Comma-separated requirements awaiting verification.

columns.name: future_requirements_currently_due
columns.description: Comma-separated future requirements due now.

columns.name: future_requirements_past_due
columns.description: Comma-separated future requirements already overdue.

columns.name: future_requirements_eventually_due
columns.description: Comma-separated future requirements eventually due.

columns.name: future_requirements_pending_verification
columns.description: Comma-separated future requirements awaiting verification.

notes: Requirements columns are comma-separated strings, not arrays. Split them with split(col, ',') to unnest.
This table contains personal data. Handle exports according to your privacy obligations.

itemized_fees.description: Granular breakdown of every fee charged or deducted from your Stripe balance, one row per fee component.

columns.name: balance_transaction_created
columns.description: Time (in UTC) at which the balance transaction affected your Stripe balance.

columns.name: balance_transaction_id
columns.description: The ID of the balance transaction that debited the fee from your balance.

columns.name: balance_transaction_description
columns.description: The description of the balance transaction containing the fee.

columns.name: incurred_by
columns.description: The ID of the object that incurred this fee, if any. Use incurred_by_type to determine the type of this object.

columns.name: incurred_by_type
columns.description: The object type which incurred_by references. Matches the object field in the API (Charge, Refund, Invoice, etc).

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Fee incurred for this activity, expressed in MAJOR units of the currency. Excludes the tax amount.

columns.name: tax
columns.description: Tax component of the fees paid, expressed in MAJOR units of the currency.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Three-letter ISO code for the currency in which amount and tax are defined.

columns.name: incurred_at
columns.description: Time (in UTC) at which the fee was incurred, by the date of its originating event.

columns.name: activity_start_date
columns.description: For fees calculated from activity spanning a period of time, the activity's starting date (UTC).

columns.name: activity_end_date
columns.description: For fees calculated from activity spanning a period of time, the activity's ending date (UTC).

columns.name: product_feature_description
columns.description: The product or feature associated with the fee.

notes: amount and tax are in MAJOR currency units here, unlike almost every other Sigma table. Do not divide by 100.
Column list is complete as published by Stripe.
